Creating Shared Value through Digital Health Ecosystem : A Case Study of Telkom Employee Social Activity to Intervention Stunting in Southwest Papua
records.venue: Poster Conference Proceeding of International Conference on Research in Emerging Technologies and Strategic Business & The 10th International Seminar and Conference on Learning Organisation (ICRES-ISCLO)
records.abstract:
Background
Stunting remains a significant challenge in Southwest Papua, with traditional community health systems ineffective in addressing child growth monitoring. This study explores how Telkom Indonesia – Witel Papua Barat, through its employee-driven Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program, implemented a collaboration quadruple helix among stakeholders—communities, government, academia, and business. This case aims to demonstrate how technology-enabled CSR can create shared social and business value by a digital application (Baby Pos) within local health ecosystems.

Abstract Purpose
- Stunting as an ongoing health challenge in Indonesia, 30.5% The highest prevalence of stunted children in Southwest Papua province is below the national 19.8%. - Weakness of the traditional Posyandu, - Unsustainable of CSR Integration. - Market penetration in West Papua is very challenging.

Design/Methodology/Approach
This study employed a single instrumental case study design (Yin, 2014; Stake, 1995) to examine Telkom Indonesia Witel Papua Barat’s TESA program as an exemplar of digital-health-ecosystem-enabled CSR intervention for stunting reduction in Sorong and Aimas districts, Southwest Papua. Data were collected over a 12-month pilot period (17 October 2024 – November 2025) using multiple sources: participant observation, semi-structured interviews, FGDs, program documents, Baby Pos app analytics. Thematic analysis using Braun & Clarke (2006) 6-phase framework.

Findings
- Cadres gained time for counseling over admin tasks ; integrated data enabled decision-making. - Students applied innovations in real settings. - TESA is an employee-leadership capability development program, built to foster employee agility and a digital working culture. - Business shift: From CSR to B2B pipeline

Research
The study was limited to a one-year pilot across five Posyandu sites, with challenges including limited internet infrastructure, data protection risk and varying levels of digital literacy among users. These factors may affect scalability and generalizability.

Originality/Value
This research demonstrates how a state-owned enterprise can transform CSR from philanthropy into a shared value strategy through digital health innovation and quadruple-helix collaboration. The Baby Pos initiative illustrates a replicable model for CSR-driven digital health interventions that simultaneously advance SDGs and business sustainability.

records.title: Cross-level pathways from teacher autonomy support to adolescent intrinsic motivation through basic psychological need satisfaction: a multilevel mediation model with classroom climate as a boundary condition
records.abstract: Introduction Teacher autonomy support is associated with adolescent intrinsic motivation, but the shared classroom context is often omitted from analyses. Drawing on self-determination theory and achievement goal theory, this study examined indirect associations through autonomy, competence and relatedness need satisfaction and their moderation by classroom motivational climate. Methods Cross-sectional questionnaire data were collected from 2,634 students in 72 secondary-school classes across grades 7–12. A two-level structural equation model with random slopes separated within-class and between-class pathways. Measurement invariance was evaluated across three grade bands. Indirect effects and pairwise contrasts were assessed using 20,000 Monte Carlo draws, and mastery and performance climates were tested as cross-level moderators. Results Scalar measurement invariance supported pooling the grade bands. All three indirect effects were positive at both levels. Within-class estimates through autonomy, competence and relatedness were 0.148, 0.102 and 0.068, respectively; between-class estimates were 0.256, 0.167 and 0.154. Explained variance in intrinsic motivation was 31% within classes and 47% between classes. Pairwise contrasts favored autonomy over the other needs, with weaker evidence for its advantage over competence; competence and relatedness were not statistically distinguishable. The between-class joint equality test was borderline. Mastery climate strengthened the first-stage autonomy and competence paths, whereas performance climate weakened them. Neither moderator was significant for the relatedness path. Discussion The findings support distinguishing individual perceptions from shared classroom conditions when studying autonomy-supportive teaching. Classroom climate may help explain variation in the associations between perceived support, need satisfaction and intrinsic motivation. Because the study was cross-sectional and relied on student self-report, the estimated indirect pathways do not establish causal or temporal ordering.

records.title: Development routes of resource and capability configurations in small and medium-sized enterprises
records.abstract:
Objective: The objective of the article is to identify and analyse the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in an international context by classifying 785 firms from eight countries into configurations based on performance across ten resource and capability pillars, linking configurations to competitiveness, and analytically inferring plausible, path-dependent development routes between them.
Research Design & Methods: We drew on the Global Competitiveness Project (GCP) dataset. We collected data between 2016 and 2020 in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Czech Republic, France, Hungary, Mexico, and Spain through structured face-to-face interviews with SME owners or top executives. We classified firms into four configurations (Balanced, Core Competence, Harmonised, Bottleneck) based on skewness and relative variance across the ten pillars, quantified using GCP interview-based measures. We applied one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and binary logistic regression models to assess configuration differences in competitiveness and to support inferences about potential development routes.
Findings: The analysis revealed statistically significant differences in competitiveness across configurations: Harmonised firms displayed the highest competitiveness, whereas Balanced firms exhibited the lowest. The models suggest two main development logics. Balanced firms may reduce pillar dispersion and strengthen Technology, Decision-making, Marketing, and Networks to move towards a Harmonised configuration, or they may prioritise Technology (and, in some cases, Decision-making and Human Capital) in ways that generate a Bottleneck configuration. Core Competence firms may move towards Bottleneck by further reinforcing Technology, or towards Harmonised by broadening and aligning key pillars. However, some transitions appear economically unattractive, as the costs of incremental configuration change may outweigh competitiveness gains.
Implications & Recommendations: SME development strategies should strengthen configuration-specific pillars. Managers can use the identified configurations to diagnose their position and prioritise targeted improvements. Policymakers and practitioners should support SMEs in recognising their configuration and implementing focused interventions that improve the effectiveness of resource and capability deployment.
Contribution & Value Added: The study adds to resource-based view (RBV) and configuration-based research on SME competitiveness by linking an established competitiveness index to a four-type configuration scheme, including a Balanced configuration. It proposes a systematic, configuration-based framework for assessing how specific pillars shape competitiveness and for analytically inferring non-linear development routes between configurations, thereby refining GCP-related evidence and offering actionable guidance for SMEs.

records.title: DIGITAL COMPETENCE OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS IN SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF RESEARCH TRENDS, CHALLENGES, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT NEEDS
records.venue: Electronic Journal of University of Aden for Humanity and Social Sciences
records.abstract: As digital technologies become increasingly embedded in English language teaching scholarly attention has focused on teachers’ digital competence and on the contextual factors that shapes its development across Arab contexts. This research paper aimed to review synthesise key trends, challenges and professional development requirements of English language teachers in relation to their digital competence in Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Using a qualitative evidence synthesis design, the study synthesized findings from 20 empirical studies published between 2013 and 2026. The review used content analysis, thematic synthesis, and contextual comparison to identify research trends, reported challenges, and professional-development needs in the two settings. Content analysis, thematic synthesis, and contextual comparative analysis were applied to integrate findings across this methodologically heterogeneous evidence base and to identify research patterns, challenges, and professional development needs specific to each context. The findings indicate a shift in research focus from technology access and basic use toward broader dimensions of digital competence, including Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK), technology-assisted language learning, digital literacy, pedagogical technology integration, and emerging digital competencies. Challenges that have been identified include lack of technological infrastructure, unreliable internet, variation in the level of teacher digital competence, problems integrating technology into the teaching of English language, lack of sufficient professional development, lack of institutional, as well as technical support, particularly in Yemen, and differences between the two countries. Significant differences can also be detected: studies in Saudi Arabia have started targeting higher levels of teacher digital competence and more innovative pedagogy, while studies in Yemen have remained more focused on more fundamental challenges of insufficient infrastructure, socio-economic difficulties, weak institutional support, and problems caused by conflict. Therefore, needs-based, ongoing, pedagogically grounded and context-specific professional development provided with the help of collaboration, mentoring, communities of practice, technical support, and institutional support are called for. The study concludes that digital competence is perceived as context-dependent multi-dimensional construct that needs to be approached through tailored interventions and policies.

records.title: Driving Value and Improving Efficiency: Digital Fuel Measurement as a Strategic Enabler in State-Owned Logistics — a Case Study of Limosin at Elnusa Petrofin
records.abstract: This study examines the digital transformation of fuel logistics within Indonesian state-owned enterprises (SOEs), focusing on the implementation of LIMOSIN (Liquid Monitoring System) at Elnusa Petrofin. Despite global advances in IoT-enabled measurement systems, Indonesian fuel distribution continues to rely on manual dipstick measurement, handwritten logs, and fragmented reconciliation processes. Using a qualitative case study approach supported by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Resource-Based View (RBV), VRIO, and Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA), this research analyzed the operational, behavioral, and strategic implications of adopting digital fuel measurement systems. Findings reveal that LIMOSIN significantly improves accuracy, transparency, and traceability but faces adoption barriers due to low perceived ease of use, limited system integration, and institutional constraints typical of SOEs. Strategically, LIMOSIN positions Elnusa Petrofin toward greater client trust and differentiation in B2B logistics. The study contributes theoretical and managerial insights into digital adoption within emerging market SOEs and provides recommendations to strengthen readiness and strategic alignment.

records.title: ENGLISH AS A FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHERS’ PERCEIVED COMPETENCE LEVELS IN USING INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY
records.venue: TNU Journal of Science and Technology
records.abstract: Nghiên cứu này nhằm tìm hiểu nhận thức của giảng viên giảng dạy tiếng Anh như một ngoại ngữ về năng lực sử dụng công nghệ thông tin và truyền thông của họ, đồng thời nghiên cứu ảnh hưởng của giới tính và độ tuổi đến năng lực này. Phiếu khảo sát dựa theo nghiên cứu của Albirini (2004) có sự điều chỉnh được dùng làm công cụ thu thập số liệu. Phiếu khảo sát gồm 02 phần: Phần 1 điều tra thông tin cá nhân của giảng viên và Phần 2 gồm 18 nhận định với 4 mức lựa chọn theo thang đo Likert. Phương pháp phân tích định lượng, số liệu thống kê mô tả và suy diễn được sử dụng để phân tích dữ liệu thu thập được từ 112 giảng viên thông qua cuộc khảo sát trực tuyến bằng Google Form. Kết quả cho thấy, mặc dù giảng viên chưa thành thạo trong một số kỹ năng cụ thể, năng lực sử dụng công nghệ thông tin và truyền thông của họ nhìn chung là thành thạo. Ngoài ra, nghiên cứu cũng chỉ ra giới tính và độ tuổi có ảnh hưởng đáng kể đến năng lực sử dụng công nghệ thông tin và truyền thông của giảng viên. Cuối cùng, nghiên cứu đưa ra một số gợi ý cho các nghiên cứu về năng lực sử dụng công nghệ thông tin và truyền thông của giảng viên.

records.title: FACTORS AFFECTING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION AMONG SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES IN SAMPHANTHAWONG DISTRICT, BANGKOK
records.venue: The EUrASEANs: journal on global socio-economic dynamics
records.abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technology among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Samphanthawong District, Bangkok - a historic commercial area undergoing digital transition. The research employs a quantitative design using survey data from 321 SME entrepreneurs, drawing upon the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), and System Quality Theory. Key variables include perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, social influence, technological experience, system quality, and organizational support. We applied hierarchical multiple regression and moderation analysis to test the direct and interaction effects. Results reveal that system quality, ease of use, and technological experience are strong predictors of AI adoption intention. Perceived usefulness becomes significant only when moderated by prior technological experience, highlighting its declining relevance among digitally mature users. Social influence was non-significant, suggesting autonomous decision-making among SME owners. Additionally, younger entrepreneurs exhibited higher AI training demands, particularly in automation and foundational skills. The findings point out that it takes intuitive AI platforms, age-sensitive training programs, and targeted policy interventions to foster inclusive digital transformation among urban SMEs.

records.title: From basic psychological need satisfaction to sense of gain: A self- determination theory framework for mental health curriculum reform in higher vocational education
From Mandatory Exposure to Guided Engagement: Investigating the Structured Integration of Generative AI in Higher Education
records.abstract: The rapid institutionalization of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created an urgent need for empirical evidence on how structured course-level integration relates to student engagement and perceptions of learning. This study examines a usefulness-centered conceptual framework combining elements of the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (TAM/UTAUT) with the digital competence perspective of DigComp 2.2. A structured pedagogical pilot intervention requiring all students to use generative AI tools was implemented in an undergraduate Public Service Management course (n = 76). Students completed AI-supported group assignments and an immediate post-intervention questionnaire comprising 19 Likert-scale items, four demographic questions, and four optional open-ended questions that are not analyzed in the present paper. Because most variables were non-normally distributed, non-parametric statistical methods were applied, including Spearman’s rank correlations, Mann–Whitney U tests, and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Perceived learning usefulness was strongly and positively associated with both frequency of AI use and satisfaction with the learning process. Ethical attitudes were also positive, but more weakly associated with frequency of use. Demographic group differences were observed mainly in specific usage patterns rather than in general attitudes towards AI-supported learning. These exploratory findings suggest that perceived learning usefulness remains relevant in mandatory AI-integration contexts. Pedagogical scaffolding—including prompt literacy, verification practices, and reflective documentation—provides a structured framework for guided and responsible use of generative AI tools in higher education.

records.title: From Output to Input: Using Echo-STT Rehearsal to Enhance L2 Listening Comprehension
records.venue: LEARN Journal : Language Education and Acquisition Research Network
records.abstract: This mixed-methods study investigated the integration of the Echo Method with speech-to-text (STT) technology to enhance TOEIC listening instruction. The intervention addresses the washback effects of high-stakes testing—the influence of TOEIC on teaching and learning—by transforming test-focused drills into authentic, learner-centered listening practice. Forty-five Applied English majors at a Taiwanese technological university participated in an 18-week intervention featuring reflective echoing, STT-based self-monitoring, and collaborative transcript analysis. Quantitative results from four diagnostic tests (normalized to a 0–100 scale) showed significant listening gains, with weighted overall means rising from 73.98 (pretest) to 87.87 (posttest) (d = 1.12). Improvements were greatest in sections with lower cognitive load: Part 1 (Picture Descriptions, d = 1.48) and Part 2 (Question-Response, d = 1.52). Regression analysis revealed that STT engagement frequency, rather than class attendance, predicted listening gains (β = .62, p < .001). Qualitative data from journals, interviews, and surveys indicated that STT feedback enhanced metacognitive awareness (73%) and reduced listening anxiety (60%) by externalizing errors in a non-judgmental format. Learners also reported perceived improvements in speaking naturalness, suggesting receptive-to-productive transfer effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that technology-enhanced articulatory rehearsal can bridge the gap between test-focused drills and communicative competence, transforming high-stakes preparation into a learner-centered experience.

records.title: Gamification in L2 Arabic Writing Instruction: Perceived Usability and Learning Support of Baamboozle in an Indonesian Islamic Secondary School Context
records.venue: ALSUNA Journal of Arabic and English Language
records.abstract:
Purpose - Arabic writing instruction in Indonesian Islamic secondary schools is still largely teacher-fronted: structured, passive, and lacking in practice that builds productive skills. This study examines whether the browser-based game platform Baamboozle can shift that dynamic. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Vygotskian scaffolding theory, and self-determination theory (SDT), we document the implementation of Baamboozle in an L2 Arabic writing class at MAPK MAN 1 Surakarta, Indonesia, and report how students evaluated its usability, visual design, interactivity, and perceived learning support across five theoretically grounded dimensions. 
Design/methodology/approach - A quantitative descriptive design was employed. Twenty female students from Class X MAPK participated in a Baamboozle-integrated Arabic writing lesson and subsequently completed a nine-item, four-point Likert-scale questionnaire mapped onto five TAM-derived perception dimensions for L2 Arabic writing development: ease of access, operability, interactivity, visual appeal, learning motivation, language clarity, and perceived effectiveness. Descriptive statistics and RAL scores were computed via IBM SPSS Statistics 22.0. This study has a bounded, exploratory design; findings are interpreted as preliminary perceptual evidence rather than causal claims about learning outcomes. 
Findings – All nine perception items fell in the excellent range (85%–100%), with an overall RAL of 87% (M = 31.65/36, SD = 3.05). Students rated perceived support for L2 Arabic writing development highest (RAL = 91%)—consistent with SDT predictions about competence-supportive task structures—while platform accessibility scored lowest (RAL = 83%), pointing to a minor entry-friction problem that is practically fixable. No item dropped below 83%, indicating that learners were broadly positive across the usability, affective, and instructional dimensions. 
Originality/value - The study contributes to CALL and L2 Arabic writing research in three ways. This study extends TAM–based technology acceptance work to a typologically complex productive-skill context (Arabic orthography) in a Southeast Asian Islamic school setting, which is rarely represented in CALL literature. This study shows how Vygotskian image-based scaffolding and SDT-aligned game mechanics can work together inside a low-cost, zero-registration platform. Furthermore, it offers a replicable four-stage implementation model that does not require specialist infrastructure. The study is bounded: n = 20, one session, self-report only. Causal claims about writing development require follow-up. 
Paper type – Research paper

records.title: Hybrid work and daily well-being: The role of need satisfaction and telework normativeness from a self-determination theory perspective
records.venue: German Journal of Human Resource Management: Zeitschrift für Personalforschung
records.abstract: Drawing on self-determination theory, this daily diary study examines why and when hybrid work relates to employees’ daily well-being. We propose that working from home versus working in the office differentially satisfies employees’ needs for autonomy, relatedness, and competence, which, in turn, are associated with daily work engagement and cognitive stress. We further examine telework normativeness—the extent to which telework is common and institutionally supported in the work unit—as a contextual boundary condition of these relationships. Multilevel structural equation models based on data from 114 employees and 744 daily observations revealed that, compared with office days, home days were associated with higher autonomy- and competence-need satisfaction but lower relatedness-need satisfaction. These need-based experiences, in turn, accounted for the indirect associations between work location and both work engagement and cognitive stress. Telework normativeness attenuated the indirect associations through autonomy and relatedness, whereas no corresponding moderation emerged for competence. Additional between-person analyses indicated that employees’ overall amount of telework was not associated with average need satisfaction, work engagement, or cognitive stress. These findings contribute to research on hybrid work by identifying distinct motivational mechanisms through which daily work location relates to well-being and by showing that these mechanisms depend partly on the normative context of telework. Overall, hybrid work is neither uniformly beneficial nor harmful: its daily implications depend on which psychological needs are supported in a given location and on how telework is embedded in the broader work context.

records.title: Implementing Used Cooking Oil to Soap Conversion and Digital Marketing in PKK RW 14 Sekeloa Bandung Indonesia
records.abstract: Community members often dispose of used cooking oil into drains, which harms local environments and misses a simple valorization pathway. This program with PKK RW 14 Sekeloa in Bandung trained 15 participants to convert used oil into household bar soap and to operate basic digital selling routines. A one-group pre and post evaluation used 5 instruments: soap-making knowledge and attitudes (5 items), behavior and readiness to adopt soap-making (5 items), post-only perceived impact and sustainability (5 items), technology use for listing and operations (19 items), and a 10-item knowledge quiz. Results show consistent improvement. On knowledge and attitudes, the largest item gain was basic soap-making steps (+40 percentage points, favorable 40% to 80%); basic processing method and economic potential increased by +27 points each, raising favorable to 93% and 80%. Item averages moved from 55% to 81% favorable. On behavior and readiness, improper disposal (reverse-scored) improved by +60 points to 93% favorable, while item averages rose from 55% to 79% favorable. Post-only perceptions were strongly positive (85% favorable on average; usefulness and environmental awareness 93% each). Technology use advanced broadly from 32% to 75% favorable on item averages, with many domains at 73-93% favorable after training; promotions and cost recording remained the weakest areas. Quiz scores improved from 6.0 ± 1.3 to 8.9 ± 0.8, with participants scoring ≥8/10 increasing from 33% to 87%. The findings indicate that a short, safety-focused curriculum coupled with simple operating standards can build procedural competence and immediate readiness for micro-enterprises and its replicability in other urban communities.

records.title: Integrating DeepL Write and Claude AI to enhance argumentative writing competence of engineering students in India
records.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly applied to support second language writing. However, empirical research examining their potential to enhance the argumentative writing skills of STEM engineering students, particularly in the English as a Second Language (ESL) context in India, remains limited and requires more exploration. Method This study employed a quasi-experimental mixed-method design to investigate the effectiveness of two AI tools, DeepL Write and Claude AI, in improving argumentative writing among 40 first-year engineering students at a private university in Chennai, India. The Toulmin model of argumentation-based rubric was used to analyse the argumentative essays written by participants before and after the intervention using the AI tools. In the quantitative phase, paired-sample t-test and one-way ANOVA were employed to analyse differences in the pre-test and post-test essay scores. These results were further explained through comparative analysis of the essay scripts (n = 40) and thematic coding of participants’ semi-structured interview data (n = 23) in the qualitative phase. Results The quantitative results demonstrate significant improvement in the AW skills of the participants (t = −43.72; df = 39; p-value < 0.001; f = 1.534; p > 0.05). The findings also indicated uniform improvements across all Toulmin components. The comparative analysis of the essays evidences the development of claims, data, warrants, backing and rebuttals, as well as improvements in linguistic features such as grammar, sentence structure and vocabulary. The thematic coding of the interview data yielded six themes related to perceived writing development, meta-cognitive awareness and the challenges and limitations of the tools. Discussion The findings indicate the pedagogical potential of integrating DeepL Write and Claude AI to improve argumentative writing skills of Indian ESL Engineering students. The findings also highlight the effectiveness of AI tools in improving linguistic features in students’ writing. By fostering responsible and informed use of digital technology in education, this study aligns with the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 (Quality Education).

Measuring Information and Communication Technology Use and Its Impact on Students’ Mathematics Achievement
records.venue: The International Journal of Science Mathematics and Technology Learning
records.abstract: In recent years, there has been growing interest in how students’ interactions with Information and Communication Technology (ICT) impact academic performance, particularly in mathematics. This quantitative study examined the relationship between students’ ICT use and mathematics performance in Türkiye, using secondary data from the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2018. The sample consisted of 6,890 15-year-old students from 186 schools. The study used the PISA 2018 student questionnaire and mathematics assessment as the main instruments. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM), and multi-group analysis was conducted to examine gender differences. The findings showed that mathematics performance was significantly related to both in-school and out-of-school ICT use. Students’ attitudes toward ICT, particularly interest and perceived competence, were also significantly associated with mathematics achievement and partially mediated the relationship between ICT use and achievement. Multi-group analysis revealed that most relationships were similar for boys and girls; however, perceived ICT competence predicted mathematics performance only among boys, and several pathways related to ICT attitudes differed by gender. These results enhance understanding of the role of ICT in mathematics achievement and offer important implications for educators and policy makers seeking to support effective ICT integration while addressing gender differences in technology engagement.

records.title: Nowe wektory zarządzania: Ekonomia behawioralna dla świadomych i różnorodnych organizacji
records.abstract:
Contemporary organizations operate under an unprecedented dynamic of social, economic, and technological change. Globalization, the digitalization of managerial processes, and the development of artificial intelligence, coupled with growing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, mean that effective management is no longer solely the domain of economic, financial, or organizational knowledge. It is becoming increasingly evident that sound managerial decisions rest on an understanding of human beings – their emotions, motivations, cognitive limitations, and needs related to security, dignity, and belonging. It is precisely this perspective – combining theoretical reflection with practical experience – that forms the guiding thread of this monograph, prepared on the basis of the 6th Scientific Conference “New Vectors of Management: Behavioral Economics for Conscious and Diverse Organizations,” held as part of the series “The Digital Society and Concepts of Organizational Management.”
As Daniel Kahneman observed, dispelling the myth of the perfectly rational consumer, in his book Thinking, Fast and Slow: “Our thinking is far more prone to error and far more susceptible to emotion than we tend to assume.” This observation, formulated over a decade ago, has gained renewed relevance today. Behavioral economics, by integrating the achievements of cognitive and social psychology with classical economic theory, provides tools for better understanding decision-making processes, social relations, and the mechanisms underlying the functioning of contemporary organizations. It also teaches that the organizations of the future should be built on a foundation of empathy, diversity, responsibility, and conscious leadership – values that run through all the chapters of this monograph.
The structure of the monograph reflects the multifaceted nature of the issues addressed – ranging from risk and digitalization, through artificial intelligence, legal regulation, geopolitics, and marketing, to diversity, employee well-being, and leadership from a cross-cultural perspective.
The opening chapter, by M. Barna and Z. Novosad, is devoted to risk management in the context of digitalization. The authors present a comparative analysis of two methods used to support decision-making under conditions of uncertainty – correlation and regression analysis, and expert assessment methods – highlighting their methodological foundations, strengths, and limitations in application to higher education. On the basis of a survey study, they identify the need to combine study with work as the most significant educational challenge.
In the second chapter, A. Dağdeviren addresses the accessibility of infrastructure for people with disabilities in the context of the Blue Flag programme criteria, examining its application on beaches in Türkiye. The author points to the need to ensure a continuous, safe route from parking areas to the water, as well as regular monitoring of infrastructure compliance with technical requirements, situating the chapter within a broader reflection on the inclusivity of public space.
The chapter by J. Kloc shifts the discussion to artificial intelligence and behavioral management. The author presents the theoretical foundations of behavioral management and analyzes the opportunities and challenges associated with the use of machine learning algorithms, predictive analytics, and recommendation systems in monitoring and shaping employee behavior. A significant part of the discussion is devoted to the ethical dimension of these solutions – the protection of privacy, algorithmic transparency, and the risk of decision-making bias. The chapter's conclusion, pointing to the need to maintain a balance between organizational effectiveness and respect for individual autonomy, resonates with the central theme of the entire monograph.
M. Nowikowska examines the relationship between legal regulation and organizational culture as determinants of the effectiveness of compliance systems. The author shows that the effectiveness of mechanisms ensuring an organization's compliance with the law and ethical standards does not stem solely from the quality of control procedures, but to a significant extent from the organizational culture within which they operate. It is emphasized that regulatory compliance is, in practice, co-shaped by the attitudes and values shared by an organization's members.
K. Palonka-Pulikowska addresses the issue of geopolitics and its growing impact on corporate management decisions. The author points to the gradual replacement of the globalization paradigm by a geopolitical approach, and to the growing importance of geoeconomics, which employs economic instruments to pursue political objectives. She analyzes the impact of sanctions, trade restrictions, embargoes, and export and import controls on the functioning of enterprises amid the transition from the existing international order toward a more fragmented and multipolar system, shaped to a large extent by the economic rivalry between the United States and China. The chapter raises the fundamental question of the limits within which a contemporary market economy can function in the face of the growing politicization of economic decisions.
M. Róg-Giacosa shifts the discussion to the level of business relationships, analyzing the determinants of exhibitors' perceived value of participation in B2B trade fairs in a declining industry, using the example of the Kids’ Time International Fair in Kielce. Using exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression, the author demonstrates that exhibitors' marketing capabilities – rather than the quality of event organization – have a stronger effect on the business outcomes achieved, although organizational quality remains important for the overall evaluation of the event and for exhibitors' willingness to recommend it.
A. Banaszak addresses the behavioral shaping of attitudes toward old age as a tool for building inclusive organizations. Using the example of an original workshop programme, “Understanding Old Age,” which employs a geriatric-experience simulator, the author analyzes the mechanisms through which experiential education reduces ageism and stereotypes concerning older people. The chapter emphasizes the role of direct experience of the limitations associated with the aging process in fostering empathy and intergenerational solidarity.
U. Anisiewicz combines a behavioral-economics perspective with an analysis of marketing communication, addressing the representation of women in advertising in the context of femvertising. Drawing on a survey study, the chapter examines the extent to which consumer responses to advertising messages that emphasize female empowerment are rational, and the extent to which they are shaped by cognitive heuristics. The chapter offers an interesting case study of how categories from behavioral economics intersect with marketing practice and the social perception of authenticity in advertising messages.
W. Bobisz addresses the topic of mobbing as a contemporary threat in the workplace, a subject of considerable importance for human resource management. The author points out that a rapidly changing labor market, pressure to meet performance targets, and evolving management styles all contribute to the intensification of pathological behaviors, the consequences of which affect not only employees' physical and mental health but also workplace atmosphere, staff turnover, and companies' financial performance.
L. Weldemichael presents the results of a study on the impact of loyalty programmes on passenger satisfaction in the airline industry. Amid strong competition from Middle Eastern and European carriers, the author examines how individual elements of a loyalty programme influence customer satisfaction.
H. Weldemichael, in turn, addresses the role of strategic management in enhancing the effectiveness of Ethiopian civil society and non-governmental organizations. The author examines these organizations' managerial practices, the relationship between strategic planning and effectiveness, the role of leadership, and the barriers that hinder the implementation of strategic management in the non-governmental sector.
T. Getahun presents a comparative analysis of the influence of national culture on the effectiveness of leadership styles in Ethiopia and Poland. D. Biały, in turn, broadens the scope of the issues discussed by introducing an original research perspective that contributes to the monograph’s exploration of the behavioral and organizational dimensions of contemporary management. The author examines the productivity paradox in organizations, focusing on the relationship between the growing number of information technology tools used in the workplace and the increasing prevalence of digital cognitive fatigue.
The monograph concludes with a chapter by J. Nowicka, devoted to the analysis and comparison of logistics processes implemented at selected historic sites in the Wałbrzych Agglomeration. The chapter examines information flows, deliveries, warehousing, transportation, and stakeholder service. Drawing on statistical methods, the author highlights the importance of historical logistics practices both for the preservation of cultural heritage and for the improvement of contemporary logistics management practices.
Although the chapters included in the monograph vary in terms of subject matter, methodology, and geographical scope, they share a common concern with understanding the mechanisms underlying human behavior in organizations and identifying ways to develop structures that are more aware, responsible, and inclusive. They contribute to the broader field of behavioral economics, understood not merely as a subdiscipline of economics but as an epistemological perspective that integrates insights from psychology, law, marketing, and management.

records.title: Organisational Drivers of Technology Adoption and Performance in Small and Medium-Scale Fashion Enterprises in Ghana
records.abstract:
Purpose: To examine how organisational drivers shape technology adoption among Small and Medium-Scale Fashion Enterprises (SMSFEs) in the Kumasi Metropolis and whether adoption translates into improved firm performance.
Methodology/Design: A quantitative research approach was employed, utilising structured questionnaires to collect data from 278 registered SMSFEs under the Ghana National Association of Garment Makers (GNAGM) and the Ghana National Tailors and Dressmakers Association (GNTDA). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis to determine the relationships between organisational factors, technology adoption, and performance outcomes.
Findings: Staff competence and leadership commitment are positive and significant predictors of technology adoption, while financial constraints hinder uptake; organisational culture shows a smaller but positive association. Adoption is, in turn, positively associated with performance, with the strongest perceived gains in operational efficiency and quality, alongside improvements in sales, competitiveness, and profitability.
Practical and Social Implications: Results indicated that owner-managers should convert intent into resourced action, earmarking budgets, assigning responsibility for system upkeep, and instituting brief, recurring skills practice tied to specific tools. At the ecosystem level, targeted finance (credit lines, grant matches, vendor-financed purchases) coupled with accessible, hands-on training through associations can lower adoption frictions and support job creation and competitiveness in the local fashion economy.
Originality: The study provides sector-specific, empirical evidence from an informal, owner-managed context, extending the TOE lens by disaggregating organisational drivers and linking them to adoption and performance in Ghana’s fashion SMEs.

records.title: Perceived Need for Competence Need Satisfaction as Predictor of Transition among form Two Students in Kisii County, Kenya.
records.venue: International journal of research and innovation in social science
records.abstract: Reported low transition among secondary a schoolstudents has drawn interest and attention among researchers. This is because transition determines how learners succeed   from one academic level to the next and how they achieve life time goals. Research was guided by Self Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan 2002). The participants were 405 students (167 males, 238 females). The participants filled questionnaire items adapted from Multidimensional Psychological Needs Satisfaction Scale. The major finding showed that there is a significant positive relationship between respondents' competence and transition. (r (403) = 0.22, p < .05).   Considering that more attention is paid to factors related to school infrastructure as students transit to secondary school, the study made some recommendations. They included encouraging students to develop inner satisfaction of Psychological needs satisfaction (competence). The researchers also recommended stakeholders to create an enabling school environment that enhance individual competence satisfaction among students. The research also recommended further research in the area of competence l needs satisfaction as a predictor of transition.

records.title: Predicting affective well-being from self-determination needs satisfaction: The moderating role of work positivities and work negativities
Preparedness for Business-Related Programs in Higher Education Among ABM Students: Basis for Intervention Programs
records.venue: International Journal of Multidisciplinary Applied Business and Education Research
records.abstract:
This study determined the extent of the business programAccountancy, Business, and Management (ABM) respondents from five public senior high schools in Quezon City, District I, were proportionally chosen through a convenient sampling technique from the total population of 471 enrollees in ABM. Using an expert-validated researcher-made questionnaire, the respondents self-assessed their level of competence in 21st-century skills, financial literacy, entrepreneurial skills, and emotional intelligence.
The students believed they were well-prepared in communication, personal responsibility, and ICT proficiency but were less prepared in applied financial skills, especially investment management and bookkeeping, and applied entrepreneurial skills, especially prototyping and business modeling. The students also perceived themselves to have moderate-high emotional intelligence, with the lowest degree in emotional regulation.
Inferential statistics using the Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis H tests yielded only two significant differences: females are more proficient in ICT than males (U = 4381.5, p = .021), and information proficiency is significantly higher in the highest income bracket than in the lowest income bracket (H = 14.104, p = .007). These two significant differences in the group indicate inequity in access to technologies and an information-rich environment at home, which the school system should address.
To address the gaps in the perceived college readiness of future business majors, the researcher proposes a two-year intervention program titled Business-Ready: Skill-Building for Future Business Majors, which uses applied learning, mentorship, and business simulation.

records.title: Psychological Need Satisfaction and Student Performance in Gamified Learning: The Mediating Role of Motivation Based on Self-Determination Theory
records.venue: International journal of research and innovation in social science
records.abstract: In higher education, gamified learning has attracted greater attention as a cutting-edge pedagogical strategy to enhance student engagement and academic achievement. However, little is known about the psychological processes underlying how gamified learning affects student outcomes. This study investigates the effects of autonomy, competence, and relatedness on student performance in a gamified learning environment, using Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and motivation as a mediating variable. Data from 201 undergraduate students who participated in gamified learning activities in a university course were collected using a quantitative research approach. To test the suggested correlations between the constructs, the data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that in gamified learning environments, student motivation is greatly influenced by autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Additionally, it was discovered that student performance was positively and significantly impacted by motivation. Additionally, the results show that motivation mediates the relationship between psychological need satisfaction and student performance. This suggests that students who feel more competent, related, and autonomous in gamified learning environments are more likely to become more motivated, which in turn improves their academic performance. By offering empirical support for the use of Self-Determination Theory in higher education, this study adds to the expanding body of research on gamified learning and student motivation. The results emphasize the importance of creating gamified learning environments that meet students' psychological needs to increase motivation and boost academic achievement. For educators and instructional designers seeking to develop more engaging and effective learning opportunities in higher education, the study offers valuable insights.

records.title: Resource Barrier Versus Resource Drain: Adult Attachment Differentially Moderates the Impact of Social Support on Well-Being Through Need Satisfaction
records.abstract: Perceived social support consistently predicts subjective well-being (SWB), yet the underlying psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions remain insufficiently understood. Integrating Conservation of Resources (COR) theory with Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study tested a moderated mediation model in which basic psychological need satisfaction (autonomy, competence, relatedness) mediates the social support–SWB relationship, with adult attachment orientations (anxiety, avoidance) as moderators. A sample of 488 Chinese university students (52.0% female; Mage = 20.15) completed self-report measures. Parallel mediation analysis showed that all three needs significantly mediated the social support–SWB link, with competence as the strongest mediator. Moderated mediation analyses showed that attachment avoidance significantly weakened the indirect effect through competence satisfaction, whereas attachment anxiety, despite significant negative main effects, did not moderate any pathway. These findings suggest that avoidance may function as a “resource barrier” that attenuates the internalization of support into need satisfaction, whereas anxiety may operate as a “resource drain,” associated with depleted baseline resources while the support-uptake mechanism remains intact. This study advances theory by proposing distinct functional roles for attachment dimensions within an integrated COR-SDT framework. Practical implications for attachment-informed, need-supportive interventions among university students are discussed.

records.title: Sales innovativeness climate and B2B salesperson performance: the roles of persistence, entrepreneurial self-efficacy and creative selling
records.abstract:
Persistence is widely viewed as essential for success in business to business (B2B) selling, yet it remains unclear how persistence translates into higher sales performance when selling requires experimentation and novel customer solutions. This study examines whether a perceived sales innovativeness climate enables persistence and entrepreneurial self-efficacy (ESE) and, in turn, creative selling, driving B2B sales performance.
 
 
 
 An online survey of 346 US-based B2B salespeople was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM).
 
 
 
 The perceived sales-innovativeness climate is positively associated with ESE, persistence, and sales performance. Persistence is positively related to sales performance and ESE, but not directly to creative selling. ESE is positively related to creative selling and sales performance, and creative selling is positively related to sales performance. Overall, the results indicate that persistence contributes to creative selling primarily via ESE rather than through a direct effect.
 
 
 
 The study is cross-sectional and relies on self-reported measures, including sales performance.
 
 
 
 Managers should cultivate a climate that supports sales innovativeness and invest in capacity-building, coaching, and experimentation routines so that sustained effort is translated into creative selling behaviors that improve performance.
 
 
 
 The study clarifies the roles of persistence and ESE in B2B sales by showing that creative selling is enabled chiefly through ESE, while persistence primarily strengthens performance and ESE rather than directly driving creativity.

records.title: The Effect of Practical Digital Marketing Training on Digital Skills, Employability, and Entrepreneurial Intention among Young People
records.venue: The Critical Review of Social Sciences Studies
records.abstract: The rapid expansion of the digital economy has increased demand for workers and entrepreneurs who can use digital platforms, interpret data, create content, manage online campaigns, and translate technology into commercial value. At the same time, many young people leave formal education with substantial theoretical knowledge but limited experience applying digital tools in realistic work settings. This paper examines the effect of practical digital marketing training on three interconnected outcomes among young people: digital skills, employability, and entrepreneurial intention. Using a structured narrative review of peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and major institutional reports, the paper evaluates evidence on experiential digital marketing education, digital competence, youth employment, and digital entrepreneurship. The review finds that practical training is most consistently associated with gains in applied digital competence when learners complete simulations, client projects, campaign design, analytics, search engine optimization, social media tasks, and other hands-on activities. Evidence also indicates that experiential learning, industry certifications, and work-related projects can strengthen job readiness by producing demonstrable skills and work samples. The relationship with entrepreneurial intention is positive but more conditional. Practical training appears to influence intention by increasing self-efficacy, perceived behavioral control, digital entrepreneurial knowledge, alertness to opportunities, and confidence in using online channels. However, meta-analytic evidence suggests that entrepreneurship education generally produces small average effects and that program quality, duration, prior intention, mentorship, and access to resources matter. The paper concludes that practical digital marketing training should be designed as an integrated employability and entrepreneurship intervention rather than a tool-focused short course.

records.title: The Effectiveness of User Interface Design in Business E-Communication
records.abstract:
This paper investigates the effectiveness of user interface (UI) design in business e-communication. The study synthesises existing theory and empirical findings to propose an integrated view of how UI design influences the efficiency, clarity, trust, and outcomes of electronic business communication (email, enterprise collaboration tools, web forms, e-commerce checkout flows, and customer service interfaces). Grounded in human–computer interaction (HCI) principles, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the paper develops a theoretical framework linking UI attributes (usability, information architecture, visual hierarchy, affordances, feedback, accessibility) to communication outcomes (message comprehension, response speed, task completion, perceived credibility). A qualitative research methodology is described for studying these relationships in business contexts, including semi-structured interviews, observation, and thematic analysis. Findings from a synthesis of qualitative studies and applied practitioner research are discussed, showing that well-designed UIs improve clarity, reduce cognitive load, increase user satisfaction, and enhance business metrics such as conversion and response rates. Key practical recommendations are provided for managers, designers, and organisations seeking to improve e-communication effectiveness through UI interventions. Limitations and avenues for future research are outlined.

Keywords: user interface design; business communication; usability; Technology Acceptance Model; e-communication; qualitative methodology; trust; user experience

records.title: The role of anthropomorphism and perceived competence in sculpting usage behaviour within railway ticket booking chatbots
records.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Technology
records.abstract:
Online ticket booking chatbots have emerged as potential transformative tools in the Indian railway sector. This study aims to examine user acceptance during the transition from human-assisted to chatbot-mediated ticketing services. Understanding this transition is essential for developing effective strategies to support chatbot adoption in emerging markets.
 
 
 
 This study used an extended technology acceptance model (TAM) framework to investigate the effects of anthropomorphic attributes, perceived competence and standard TAM elements on attitudes, consumer innovativeness and usage behaviour. Data from 710 respondents were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling.
 
 
 
 The analysis revealed a robust correlation between attitudes and consumer innovativeness, significantly influencing the usage behaviour of chatbot services for railway ticket booking. Moreover, demographic variations, particularly age distinctions (Gen Z/ Non-Gen Z) and gender (male/female), were considered to elucidate the unique patterns in usage behaviour.
 
 
 
 Theoretical implications include the examination of usage behaviour in railway chatbots using the TAM framework, the identification of the roles of anthropomorphism and perceived competence in chatbot usage behaviour and the exploration of the impact of attitude and consumer innovativeness on usage behaviour.
 
 
 
 This study contributes a novel perspective to academic discourse by comprehensively exploring the interplay between attitudes, consumer innovativeness and usage behaviour within the context of railway chatbots. Furthermore, its practical implications underscore its intrinsic value in informing strategic decision-making processes and fostering innovation in the railway sector.
